title: Imbalances checklist

D0.outcome: Names the main ways two sides can differ (material, minor pieces, pawn structure, space, files, initiative) and says the checklist feeds a judgement and is not a verdict.

D1.outcome: Fills the checklist for a quiet position and states which imbalance matters most for the plan.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, says which side has the easier game and why, and picks the plan that uses the favourable imbalance.

D3.outcome: Predicts how a single change flips the balance, and spots a case where the formal count says 'ahead' but the position is worse (a fictitious gain).

misconceptions: Ahead in force, space and time means winning.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S5 (Silman imbalances, [R] in the map)
sources/sheets/znosko-borovsky_middle-game.md §4 C01, C04, C05, C07; §7 rows C01-C07
conditions: The formal count is reliable only when the three counts agree and nothing tactical hangs.
The elements usually pull against each other; the job is to see which advantage the position makes possible.
contrasts: Ahead in force, space and time and still lost to one concrete idea (a rook sacrifice on the g-file).
A lead in 'time' that was made of rim-pawn pushes.
A tactical position decided by forcing moves, where the checklist is moot.
contrast_sources: ZB C01 (g); C06; Diagrams XXXVIII, XLIV
